intro: A retrieval system searches passages, not entire books. Chunk size and overlap decide how much context each searchable passage contains.
task: Split text on whitespace and return overlapping windows joined with single spaces, preserving word order.
requirements: chunk_size must be a positive integer; overlap must be an integer from 0 through chunk_size-1. Booleans are invalid.
Advance by chunk_size - overlap words. Stop after emitting a window that reaches the final word.
Return [] for empty or whitespace-only text. Do not emit a trailing window entirely contained in the previous window.
Reject non-string text or invalid settings with ValueError. This exercise counts words, not model tokens.

examples.name: Overlap
examples.input: text='a b c d e', chunk_size=3, overlap=1

examples.name: No overlap
examples.input: text='a b c d e', chunk_size=2, overlap=0

hints.title: Normalize whitespace
hints.body: str.split() without a separator handles spaces, tabs, and newlines.

hints.title: Calculate the stride
hints.body: The start position advances by size minus overlap.

hints.title: Stop at the end
hints.body: After each chunk, check whether its end reached the word count before advancing.

explanation: Overlap gives neighboring chunks shared context. Too much overlap increases duplication and indexing cost.
Determinism matters: the same text and settings should produce the same chunk boundaries every time.
Word chunking is a useful baseline. A production system may also need token budgets, sentence boundaries, metadata, and document-specific parsing.
